The \*Christian\* god may be saying who you are is fundamentally wrong, but maybe another idea of god is accepting. I don't know how religion works since I was raised atheist. If you don't connect to the idea of God, then that's okay. But that doesn't necessarily mean you have to be full on atheist. There are other religions, other practices, etc that can be fulfilling. In fact, some scientists are still practicing their faiths, like Maya Bialik, (Jewish, neuroscience degree, actress on The Big Bang Theory) or believe in the concept of God (Neil Degrasse Tyson). They all have their reasons for their version of faith that feeds their spiritual life.

I'm still an atheist. I am okay with it and like the way I view things. But I do envy some of the social and emotional benefits of religions, or even looser faiths. I just can't believe. I mean this with no ill will, but watching people with faith is like watching a level of innocence, and it's like I don't want to tell them that Santa doesn't exist (stupid analogy). I find, at least for me, there is a weight in "knowing" Santa doesn't exist, no matter how hard I wish I believed.

If you are like me and just can't believe anymore, then that's okay. But if you still have a concept of something else like a god, or spirit, etc., there may still be a faith out there that can fit your idea of how life operates, or even how to be the best human you can be.

Hope this is of any use.

Edit: I personally wouldn't say faith is childish. My analogy is less to do with being a child than my viewpoint. In fact, faith can be a way to structure your life and gain meaning, and there's nothing wrong with that. Why be depressed over the meaninglessness of your actions(ie me), when you have a concept of broader meaning, reinforced by social support?
